description:
`./dev`'s libghostty step runs `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Demit-xcframework=true -Dxcframework-target=native -Demit-terminfo=true`. At the pinned commit (9f9b8d1), Ghostty's `src/build/Config.zig` defaults `-Demit-macos-app` to `!emit-lib-vt and emit-xcframework`, so that one call also runs xcodebuild on Ghostty's whole macOS app and installs the result. Muster links only the xcframework.

Each build leaves two copies of the app in the checkout:

- `deps/ghostty/macos/build/ReleaseLocal/Ghostty.app`, xcodebuild's output
- `deps/ghostty/zig-out/Ghostty.app`, the copy `macos_app.install()` makes (build.zig:242)

Both carry the bundle id `com.mitchellh.ghostty` and version 0.1. Seen 2026-10-27 on the owner's laptop: Alfred lists both beside `/Applications/Ghostty.app` when searching "ghostty". Inferred, not seen: Launch Services registers them too, so something that opens Ghostty by bundle id could start a dev build instead of the installed one.

What it costs besides the clutter:

- An xcodebuild of a whole app on every libghostty rebuild, which happens on a re-pin or a patch edit. Not measured.
- CI caches `zig-out` (the comment at `./dev`'s restore step says so), so the app rides in that cache too.

Likely fix: pass `-Demit-macos-app=false` on that `zig build` line, then confirm GhosttyKit's xcframework still builds and the shell still links. No commit here records a reason for building the app.
title: 🍏 Every libghostty build also builds Ghostty.app, and leaves two copies Spotlight finds
